summary: The utility sandbox: when no registered tool fits, a small Python utility is drafted (by the desk from your words, by the model through the turn kind UTILITY, or written by you), shown with what it reads and writes, the seal and what the desk saw in its text, and run only sealed on copies: its own network namespace (checked: loopback only), Landlock (its folder; Python's libraries read-only; no execute; checked it cannot list Files or read /etc/passwd), seccomp (no socket, no program, no new process), CPU/memory/file/wall limits. Its output, what the seal stopped, and each output against the original are shown; Apply (approve scope, in ALWAYS_ASKS) asks at every place of the dial and makes a new revision, verified on disk and recorded through L4, refused if the file changed since the copy. A kept utility becomes a registered tool (101 up) with its own grant. HALT ends running utilities (K3 halt_gate hook) and none starts while it holds. A centre tab in every look; Tools > A Utility on Copies…

decisions: Operations named sandbox.* (status, list, get, draft, seen, run, close, apply, keep); apply and keep are approve scope and in stacy_hand.ALWAYS_ASKS.

Seccomp added to the seal beyond the brief: a network namespace alone leaves filesystem Unix sockets (the session D-Bus) reachable; the call filter refuses every socket, execve, fork/vfork and non-thread clone. Every seal is checked before the utility starts; any that does not take ends the run (never unsealed).
Python's own libraries (sys.path, LIBDIR, /usr/lib, /lib, /lib64) are readable read-only so the utility can import the standard library; nothing else outside its folder. No execute right anywhere.
The audit hook only records what the utility tried (words for the owner); the kernel seals are what refuse it (the smoke shows the utility itself seeing PermissionError).
Only a run that finished inside its seal and made a change can be applied; a stopped or failed run is shown but not offered to Apply.
A run needs the utility to have been shown (sandbox.seen, called by the window when it displays the text) and, from the window, the digest of the text shown.

The model's draft is a turn kind UTILITY: switch talk, Stop only (no grammar: code does not fit a grammar under the answer cap), answer cap 600 tokens; parsed as Python and looked at by the desk; marked "drafted by the model" (model_words.MARKS["DRAFTED"], added at run time from my module, model_words.py untouched).

Kept utilities are tools utility.<name>, numbered from 101 per workspace, registered into K2's TOOLS by register_kept() (on keep, on sandbox.list); their arguments are kept (their own key) and inputs.

The window: a centre tab marked as a room (never the Preview), not reopened at the next start; Apply's and Keep's questions are an inline band (no modal dialog), the other buttons hidden while it is up, Cancel focused.
bubblewrap is the fallback when Landlock is missing (workshop_sandbox.base_argv); not exercised here (no bwrap on this machine).
K3 (merged on main after this tree was made): halt_gate.register_stop and halt_gate.held through guarded imports; exercised in the smoke with K3's five files copied into the throwaway copy only.
findings_for_the_coordinator: K3 grants.targets() does not read sandbox.run's "inputs" list, so no grant can cover sandbox.run: through tools.use and as an assignment step it always stops as "needs your grant" (even your press on a step, since _fixed_targets is None). Fail closed, but "try utilities on copies" cannot be granted. Suggested in grants.py: targets(): if operation == 'sandbox.run': paths += [_clean_path(p) for p in a.get('inputs') or () if isinstance(p, str)] (and the same in _fixed_targets); OP_WORDS['sandbox.run'] = 'try utilities on copies of files'. The window's Run is your press through kernel.dispatch and is not affected.

K4: when no registered tool fits, utility_sandbox.draft(kernel, principal, objective, paths, request=...) drafts one and utility_sandbox_qt.show_utility(host, utility) shows it; a kept utility's step names its own key in "kept"; call utility_sandbox.register_kept(kernel) before building the numbered menu so kept utilities are listed.
Stop all spares the sandbox (its run has a session of its own, halt_gate.spared); the 30 s wall limit ends it, and HALT ends it at once.
Merge: engineering_kernel.py, engineering_cli.py and activity.py blocks sit right after K2's, beside K3's and K5's (union merge).
not_done: Nothing was tested in the owner's sense and nothing ran on the ThinkPad; a real model was not loaded (the fake worker drafted the model's utility).
The bubblewrap fallback (a computer with no Landlock) and the CLONE_NEWUSER path (an ordinary user, not root) were not exercised here: the build machine runs as root with Landlock ABI 7.
No grant covers sandbox.run until grants.targets() reads its inputs (finding above).
The panel shows a utility's text read-only; editing a draft in the window is not built (the owner's own text goes through sandbox.draft's source).
release_note: The utility sandbox: when no tool of hers fits, Kasandra can draft a small Python utility (or the desk drafts one from your words, with no model). You see it first, with what it reads and writes; it runs only sealed, on copies, with no network, no other folder and no other program, within time and memory limits. Its output and its difference to your files are shown, and applying it to your real files always asks; a utility you keep becomes a tool of yours with its own grant. Tools > A Utility on Copies…
